BankAccount.description: Stores information about bank accounts used for fee payments.

currency.description: The currency of the bank account (e.g., USD, ZWG).

tuitionOwing.description: The amount the student owes for tuition fees.

buildingFundOwing.description: The amount the student owes for the building fund.

FeesPayment.title: FeesPayment
FeesPayment.description: Stores records of student fees payments.

id.description: Unique identifier for the fees payment record.

paymentDate.description: The date the payment was made.

feeType.description: The type of fee paid (e.g., levy, tuition, building fund, exam fee).

currency.description: The currency in which the payment was made (e.g., USD, ZWG).

usdAmount.description: The equivalent USD amount (after conversion, if necessary).

recordedById.description: The ID of the user who recorded the payment.

recordedBy.description: The name of the user who recorded the payment.

TermBilling.title: TermBilling

id.description: Unique identifier for the term billing record.

term.description: The term for which the billing applies (e.g., 'Fall 2024').

tuition.description: The tuition amount for the term.

buildingFund.description: The building fund amount for the term.

Note.description: A simple note left by a user.

authorId.description: The ID of the user who created the note.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the note was created.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to address the 'permission-denied' error when listing 'bankAccounts' and to support the application's core features, emphasizing security, scalability, and ease of debugging.  The structure prioritizes authorization independence by avoiding hierarchical authorization dependencies, ensuring atomic operations and simplified debugging.

To address the immediate 'permission-denied' error, the structure places bank accounts under a dedicated collection with clearly defined access rules.  Since it is not clear from the prompt who owns the bank accounts I have to assume that the roles who can access are globally defined. Therefore the bank account will be placed in a simple roles based access collection.

Authorization Independence:  All collections avoid the need for `get()` calls in security rules. For example, student documents store all necessary information for calculating fees and owing amounts, so we do not need to read other collections.

QAPs (Rules are not Filters):  The structure is designed to allow secure `list` operations. For example, listing bank accounts is restricted to users in the `/roles_bursar/{uid}` role, preventing unauthorized access to sensitive data.

Structural Segregation: Data with different access requirements are stored in separate collections.  For instance, student data (`/students/{studentId}`) is separated from bank account data (`/bankAccounts/{bankAccountId}`), each with its own security rules.

Access Modeling:  The structure uses path-based ownership for student-related data (`/students/{studentId}/feesPayments/{feesPaymentId}`) and role-based access control for administrative data (`/roles_bursar/{uid}`). The membership map pattern is used where collaborative access is needed, although it is not present in the request, this allows it to scale in the future.

Explicit State Modeling: Student records include fields like `levyOwing`, `tuitionOwing`, and `buildingFundOwing` to explicitly track the student's financial state, making it easier to manage and query fee-related data.
